title: Prawn Bhuna
subtitle: Prawns dry-fried with spices and a thick, clinging tomato sauce
excerpt: King prawns cooked with a thick, intensely spiced sauce that clings to each prawn rather than pooling on the plate. The bhuna technique means frying off the sauce until most of the liquid has gone.
sourceNotes: Bhuna refers to a dry-frying technique common across Indian subcontinental cooking; adapted here for king prawns.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The bhuna sauce base keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Add the prawns and finish just before eating.

content.text: Bhuna means the sauce is cooked until almost dry, so the spices concentrate and coat the prawns rather than swim around them. Use a wide pan and high heat, and do not add any water or stock once the tomatoes go in. The prawns finish cooking in the dry, sticky sauce.
Heat the oil in the wok over a high heat. Add the onions and cook for 10 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden and starting to catch at the edges.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the garlic, ginger, and green chilli and stir for 1 minute.
Add the cumin, coriander, turmeric, chilli powder, and paprika. Stir for 1 minute, adding a splash of water if the spices start to stick.
Add the tomato puree and stir for 1 minute, then add the tinned tomatoes. Turn the heat up to medium-high.
Cook the tomato sauce for 15 minutes, stirring often, until it has reduced to a thick paste and the oil has separated and risen to the surface.
Turn the heat to high. Add the prawns and toss to coat in the sauce. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the prawns are pink and just cooked.
Add the garam masala and salt. Toss once more. Scatter with coriander and serve immediately.

items.symptom: The sauce is still watery after 15 minutes.
items.cause: The heat was too low to drive off the liquid quickly.
items.fix: Turn the heat to high and keep stirring. The water needs to evaporate fully before the oil will separate.

items.symptom: The spices caught on the bottom before the tomatoes went in.
items.cause: The pan was too dry or the heat too high at that stage.
items.fix: Add a small splash of water as soon as the spices smell toasted; stir quickly and add the tomato puree.

items.symptom: The prawns released water and made the sauce wet again.
items.cause: The prawns were frozen and not fully thawed and patted dry.
items.fix: Thaw prawns completely, drain, and pat dry with kitchen paper before they go in. Add them to the hottest part of the wok.
